gaps.sentence: Many consumers now opt ___ cheaper brands.
The security guard waved us ___ without checking our passes.
gaps.explanation: 'Wave somebody through' = signal them to pass a checkpoint.

gaps.sentence: Small suppliers are struggling to keep their heads ___ water.
gaps.explanation: 'Keep your head above water' = just manage to survive, especially financially.

gaps.sentence: The negotiators refused to give ___ to the hijackers' demands.
gaps.explanation: give in (to) = stop arguing and accept; give up = quit.

gaps.sentence: Police are looking ___ the cause of the crash.
Wake ___ — you'll be late for school!
I'll pay you ___ as soon as I get paid.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody back = return borrowed money; pay off a debt = finish paying it.
